app_summary: An online shop selling astronomy products, based on the OpenTelemetry Demo. It is built with polyglot microservices (Go, Java, .NET, Python, Node.js, Rust, ...) communicating via gRPC and HTTP behind an Envoy frontend-proxy, with Kafka for asynchronous order processing and Valkey as cart store. Supported Operations: View product catalog, Receive product recommendations and ads, Add item to cart, Checkout with selected items, Currency conversion, Process payment, Generate shipping quotes, Send order confirmation emails

rca_analyses_list.diagnosis: Hypothesis disproved — image-provider pod image-provider-79dbdd7cf4-hjdkw is not exhibiting consistent ~10s request-side blocking. The pod’s access logs contain only normal 200 responses and no repeated 'fetch/download/timeout/WARN/error' messages indicating ~10s remote fetches or internal queuing, and filtered logs returned no important slow-fetch entries. Metrics for the last 30 minutes show low memory (~4–6MB), modest CPU accumulation without spikes or throttling, low thread count (23), and steady high network transmit/receive consistent with serving image data (large byte counters) rather than blocking; there are no repeated ~10s CPU or network gaps that would indicate synchronous remote waits or queuing.
rca_analyses_list.reasoning: 1) Logs: Filtered log search for fetch|download|timeout|error|WARN returned no matches and full pod logs are plain HTTP access logs with frequent 200 responses (no slow-fetch or timeout entries). 2) Metrics: container_cpu_usage and container_cpu_user/system totals increase steadily but show no sharp CPU or idle patterns consistent with ~10s blocking; container_memory_usage is well below limit; container_threads remains stable at 23; container_cpu_cfs_* and throttling metrics are null (no throttling). 3) Network: container_network_transmit_bytes_total and receive counters steadily grow (large byte volumes), indicating the pod is actively serving images (IO-bound but continuous), not stalled waiting on remote fetches. Combined, logs + metrics provide no unique evidence of repeated ~10s request-side blocking in image-provider; investigate upstream (frontend/Envoy), tracing instrumentation, or network path for the observed ~10,000ms traces.

insights: Pod logs show only standard HTTP access entries with frequent 200 responses; no 'fetch', 'download', 'timeout', 'WARN', or 'error' entries were found in the last 500 lines.
Filtered log search returned no important slow-fetch or timeout messages, disproving the presence of repeated ~10s operations visible in application logs.
Container memory usage is low (~4–6 MB) and well under the 50 MB limit; working set and RSS are stable, indicating no memory pressure.
Container thread count is stable at 23 and far below the threads_max limit, so no thread explosion or obvious concurrency issue is present.

CPU metrics (user/system/total) increase steadily without sharp gaps or spikes; no CPU throttling metrics were reported (container_cpu_cfs_* are null), indicating no evidence of blocking or throttling patterns consistent with repeated 10s waits.
Network transmit/receive byte counters show steady, large growth consistent with actively serving image data (high IO throughput) rather than stalled remote fetches; packet errors/drops are zero.
Combined logs + metrics provide no evidence that image-provider is performing synchronous remote fetches or internal queuing that cause consistent ~10s request-side blocking.

Conclusion: Hypothesis that image-provider pod is the source of consistent ~10s blocking is disproven. Investigation should move upstream (frontend/Envoy), examine distributed tracing, or inspect network path and client-side behaviour for the reported ~10,000 ms traces.

Metrics for the last 30 minutes show low memory (~4–6MB), modest CPU accumulation without spikes or throttling, low thread count (23), and steady high network transmit/receive consistent with serving image data (large byte counters) rather than blocking; there are no repeated ~10s CPU or network gaps that would indicate synchronous remote waits or queuing.

Combined, logs + metrics provide no unique evidence of repeated ~10s request-side blocking in image-provider; investigate upstream (frontend/Envoy), tracing instrumentation, or network path for the observed ~10,000ms traces.
